# Water

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Water")`

A body of water: a sea, a pool, a lake or a river. Its `WaterWave` children define the waves, and the same waves are used for the simulation and for the picture, so objects float on the surface that is drawn.

An unanchored part in the water is held up by the water it displaces, sampled at points over its shape, so a hull pitches and rolls. `Viscosity` slows the part and `Current` carries it. `GetHeightAt` returns the height of the surface for a game's own use.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BankWidth` | `number` | `2` | read/write | The width of the bank that `Carve` cuts, in meters. The bed slopes from the surface at the water's edge down to the water's depth over this distance. At 0 the bank is a vertical wall. |
| `Current` | `vector` | `vector.create(0, 0, 0)` | read/write | The velocity at which the water flows, in meters per second. It carries floating objects. A `River` adds `FlowSpeed` along its course. |
| `Density` | `number` | `1` | read/write | The density of the water, in the same units as `BasePart.Density`. A part less dense than the water floats, and a part of half the water's density floats half submerged. |
| `FlowSpeed` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How fast a river flows along its points, from the first to the last, in meters per second, where it is level. Where it descends it flows faster, by four times its slope: twice as fast on a slope of one in four. |
| `Position` | `vector` | `vector.create(0, 0, 0)` | read/write | The center of a `Pool`, on the horizontal plane. Its height is set by `SurfaceLevel`. |
| `Shape` | `Enum.WaterShape` | `Enum.WaterShape.Ocean` | read/write | The extent of the water. `Ocean` is everywhere, `Pool` is a rectangle, `River` runs along its `WaterPoint` children, and `Lake` fills the closed curve through them. |
| `Size` | `vector` | `vector.create(64, 8, 64)` | read/write | The dimensions of the water, in meters. For a `Pool`: its width, its depth below the surface and its length. For a `River`: X is the width and Y the depth at any point that does not set its own. For a `Lake`: Y is the depth, and the outline comes from its points. Y must be greater than 0; X and Z can be 0. |
| `SurfaceLevel` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The height of the still surface, in meters. The waves rise and fall around it. |
| `Viscosity` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How much the water slows what moves through it. 0 is no drag, 1 suits a sea, and higher values suit a swamp. |

## Methods

### `Carve(): number`

Cuts a bed for this water into the terrain under it and returns the number of columns it lowered. Every column of ground the water covers is lowered to the bed, which slopes from the surface at the water's edge down to the water's depth over `BankWidth`. Ground that is already lower is not changed. A river's bed follows the river downhill.

An `Ocean` carves nothing. Carving only removes ground, so after moving the water, call it again to cut the new bed.

### `GetHeightAt(position: vector): number?`

Returns the current height of the surface above a position, including waves, or nil if this water does not cover the position. It matches the surface that is drawn.

### `GetNormalAt(position: vector): vector?`

Returns the direction the surface currently faces above a position, or nil if this water does not cover the position.
